newsitem.title: USA: US court delays ruling on NationsBank merger stay.
newsitem.headline: US court delays ruling on NationsBank merger stay.

text.p: DENVER, Dec 30, Reuter - A federal appeals court on Monday ordered written arguments to be submitted by Thursday on an emergency request to temporarily block NationsBank Corp's acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
The U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver took the action in response to a request last week by advocacy groups that an emergency stay of the acquisition be issued no later than Monday.

The groups wanted a stay to block the acquisition until the court could rule on their request to overturn the approval of the purchase. The board of governors of the Federal Reserve System on December 16 approved the acquisition.

The advocacy groups are the Inner City Press/Community on the Move of New York City, which represents Latinos and African-American banking consumers, and the New Mexico Alliance, which represents Mexican-Americans and native Americans.
The $9.8 billion transaction by the Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank would involve 600 branch banks operated by St. Louis-based Boatmen's and its subsidiaries, including Sunwest Banks of New Mexico.
The advocacy groups told the court the acquisition could take effective on Tuesday under terms of the Federal Reserve's approval.

A two-judge panel gave no reason for not responding to the request for a temporary stay effective Monday. But the judges, in a two-page order, noted that NationsBank had advised the court that the transaction would not close until January 7.
New Mexico is part of the 10th Circuit court's area of jurisdiction. The alliance is represented by Northern New Mexico Legal Services.
